expectations.text: The ADR states context, decision, alternatives, and consequences distinctly
expectations.evidence: Write tool created docs/decisions/ADR-001-event-sourcing-for-orders-service.md with explicitly separated headings: '## Status', '## Date', '## Context' (mutable rows, best-effort webhooks, auditor/support requirements, constraints), '## Decision' (adopt event sourcing, append-only stream as system of record), '## Alternatives Considered', and '## Consequences'. Each section contains only its own content with no bleed-over.

expectations.text: Trade-offs and rejected options are recorded, not just the winning choice
expectations.evidence: The Alternatives Considered section documents all three options from decision-context.md with Pros/Cons and an explicit disposition line: audit table ('Rejected: Auditors need history to be the source of truth, not a secondary record that can silently diverge'), CDC ('Rejected: ... a physical changelog does not answer their questions'), and event sourcing ('Cons: Introduces projection rebuilds, event schema versioning, and eventual consistency ... Accepted: ...'). Downsides of the winning option are also carried into Consequences (eventual consistency, versioning via upcasting, rebuild procedures).

expectations.text: The document is written in timeless language describing current state
expectations.evidence: Prose is present-tense and state-describing: 'The orders service stores mutable order rows and emits best-effort webhooks', 'Order state transitions are recorded as an append-only stream of domain events, which is the system of record', 'The event stream becomes the system of record for orders'. No meeting-narrative or dated storytelling ('we discussed on Tuesday', 'options were debated'); the source file's 'Options discussed:' framing was rewritten into neutral alternative descriptions. Only minor forward-looking phrasing ('needs to be validated ... before rollout', 'can be replaced'), which reads as consequence/follow-up rather than temporal narration.
